newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Nobel prize has not helped Timorese, laureate says.
newsitem.headline: Nobel prize has not helped Timorese, laureate says.

text.p: Bishop Carlos Ximenes Belo was quoted as saying on Wednesday that the award of his 1996 Nobel peace prize had not contributed to end suffering in East Timor.

"On the contrary, it has generated more distrust, and young people (Timorese) continue to be beaten and taken prisoner," the Portuguese news agency Lusa quoted Belo, bishop of Dili, as saying at a ceremony to honour him at a Lisbon university.

Belo, who visited Portugal to attend ceremonies at the Catholic shrine of Fatima marking the 80th anniversary of the "apparition" of the Virgin Mary to three Portuguese children, won the prize with Timor resistance leader Jose Ramos Horta.

Indonesia invaded the former Portuguese colony of East Timor in December 1975 and still maintains a heavy military presence there. It unilaterally annexed the territory in July 1976 in an act not recognised by the United Nations.
